title: Config change autopilot with safety harness and state harmonization
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: build an autonomous config-change autopilot that applies operational config deltas (batching, cache, routing, autoscale) with conservative guardrails and an automated reconciliation-driven rollback flow. The system should integrate with the batching/caching recommendation engine to safely apply cost-saving changes and provide deterministic, auditable reversion if QoS or cost regressions are detected. This ticket covers: 1) trigger predicates (safety and economic), 2) pre-apply dry-run and policy simulations, 3) staged rollout and canary policy, 4) automated rollback orchestration with hysteresis, 5) state harmonizer that ensures actual cluster and control-plane state converge to the expected config after partial failures, and 6) Console hooks (alerts, diff viewer, audit trail).
background: We already run a recommendations pipeline that proposes batching and prefix/KV cache profiles per model/route. Applying those changes automatically is high ROI but high risk: subtle latency tail increases or cache-miss regressions can degrade customer SLAs. Manual review is slow and doesn't scale. Several prior tickets implemented parts of rollback and safety scaffolding (see dependencies). This ticket synthesizes them into a single autopilot with richer triggers and reconciliation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Autopilot can take a recommended config bundle and run a simulated dry-run producing a policy report (latency/cost delta estimates, confidence) before real apply.
A2: Config applies can be performed as a staged rollout: canary (1% of traffic), ramp to 10%, then ramp to 100% with configurable pause windows and manual-override options.

A3: Safety triggers will automatically rollback an applied change if any of the following occur within the rollback window: p95 latency increase >20% absolute, error rate increase >1% (absolute), token-cost per 1M tokens increases >10%, or anomaly score from monitoring >0.85.
A4: Rollback action is idempotent and returns system to pre-apply desired state within the rollback hysteresis timeout (config-state reconciliation confirms convergence).
A5: All actions (apply, simulate, rollback, overrides) are logged and surfaced in Console with diff view and link to the originating recommendation.
implementation_notes: Use existing recommendations API as source-of-truth for candidate bundles; tag bundles with provenance id and confidence score.
Dry-run: run a simulated KV/batch sizing and execute cost/latency model on historical traffic windows (last 24h + 7d baseline) to produce conservative deltas.
Canary routing: implement lightweight router flag + header-based sampling to direct % traffic to canary runtime pods to avoid infrastructure churn.
Rollback orchestration: leverage existing reconcile loop but extend with transactional semantics (apply-id) and a rollback coordinator that tracks state and reasons.

State harmonizer: periodic reconciliation job that compares control-plane desired configs, runtime-local configs, and cache states (prefix cache versions), then enqueues healing steps when drift is detected.
Hysteresis: require N consecutive breach windows (configurable, default 2) before auto-rollback to reduce noisy reversions.
Testing: build canary in staging that mirrors production traffic shape using playback traces and synthetic tail-latency events.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged deployment to staging with simulation-only mode for 2 weeks.
Phase 1: Enable canary 1% for non-critical internal customers; monitor for 72 hours.
Phase 2: Ramp to 10% for broad internal + low-risk external customers; run regression/eval suite and invite SME review; 7-day observation window.
Phase 3: Default on for recommendations with high-confidence score >=0.9; lower-confidence bundles require manual approval.
Phase 4: Open autopilot for self-serve opt-in orgs; add kill-switch on org-level in Console.
test_plan: Unit: simulate dry-run reports for a matrix of recommendation deltas and validate cost/latency model outputs against ground truth traces.
Integration: deploy autopilot to staging cluster; run traffic replay with injected kernel-level slowdowns to ensure rollback triggers fire and reconcilers restore state.
Chaos: introduce partial apply failures (pod crash, API timeout) and assert state harmonizer converges desired<->actual within 10 minutes.
E2E: smoke test Console diff + audit trail links for every apply and rollback event.
Performance: validate autopilot controller CPU/memory is <10% of a single control-plane node under typical apply rate (<= 10 applies/min).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives cause unnecessary rollbacks and churn. Mitigation: hysteresis windows + require multiple breach dimensions or human-in-the-loop for low-confidence bundles.
Risk: State drift due to partial failures leaves runtime in inconsistent state. Mitigation: idempotent apply/rollback APIs and a reconciler with exponential backoff and explicit repair actions.
Risk: Cost-model inaccuracies under varied prompt distributions. Mitigation: use conservative upper-bound estimates in autopilot and prefer cache increments before aggressive quantization changes.
Risk: Security/privilege escalation via autopilot. Mitigation: RBAC checks, signed bundle provenance, and audit logging; security review required.
open_questions: Q1: What should the default confidence threshold be for fully automated (no human approval) applies? (proposal: 0.90)
Q2: How long should the rollback window be by default? (proposal: 24 hours with 2h aggressive-check intervals)
Q3: Do we surface an aggregated economic impact forecast (3-30 day savings) in Console prior to apply?
Q4: Should rollback triggers include model-quality regressions (semantic evals) for chat routes, and where do we plug those signals in?
